title: DeepCOPD: Development and Implementation of Deep Learning to Predict and Prevent COPD Health Care Encounters
text:
The proposed program in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) will provide actionable tools and
information from health care data and machine learning to identify early and prevent COPD disease
progression and major adverse health care encounters. The risk tools will be used in every day out-patient
health care practice to help prevent disease progression requiring home oxygen use, major adverse health
care encounters, and improve health care delivery for patients living with COPD in the community.

title: Engineering the degradation of decellularized plant scaffolds for hard tissue engineering
text:
PROPOSAL NARRATIVE
There is a critical need for tissue-engineered substitutes due to the chronic shortage of donor tissues for
craniofacial reconstruction. Although they are attractive platforms for tissue engineering, the main challenge of
using decellularized plant scaffolds is their limited degradation in humans, which is essential for enhancing
regenerated tissue quality. This project will develop a technique to control the degradation of decellularized plant
scaffolds through ultrasound-triggered cellulase release from microbubbles and AI/machine learning-driven,
image-guided monitoring of degradation levels.

title: UCSF Specialized Programs of Research Excellence (SPOREs) in Prostate Cancer
text:
The UCSF Prostate Cancer SPORE seeks to reduce the morbidity and mortality associated with prostate cancer
by leveraging a deep understanding of the disease to translate biological findings into clinical impact. In this
SPORE application, three translational projects focus on developing novel biomarkers and highly effective
therapies for patients with aggressive prostate cancer. These projects are highly collaborative with respect to
the multidisciplinary nature and expertise of the Co-Leaders.

title: Circulating cell-free DNA methylation as an accurate tool for detection and clinical follow-up of glioma
text:
Malignant gliomas, which include glioblastoma, account for 46.6% of primary (de novo) brain tumors that often
progress or recur as a more aggressive phenotype and are nearly uniformly fatal. Currently, the monitoring of
recurrence and progression is performed by imaging which is limited by its sensitivity, dependent on the tumor
size-threshold, the lack of specific criteria to diagnose and/or differentiate glioma from other conditions (e.g. CNS
lymphoma, pseudoprogression or radiation necrosis), and availability and feasibility for some patients. This study
proposes to establish a non-invasive approach using DNA methylation to improve detection and surveillance of
glioma, with the ultimate goal of fine-tuning treatment by providing insight into the evolving tumor biology in real
time.

title: Improve Electrical Integration of hiPSC-derived cardiac tissue with Host Heart
text:
The adult human heart cannot regenerate the cardiomyocytes to repair damaged myocardium following injury, which
may eventually lead to heart failure.
Cardiac cell therapy through implanting engineered cardiac tissue derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells
into the damaged host heart has shown promising therapeutic effects, but the electrical integration between the
implanted engineered tissue and the host heart, a key issue in cardiac cell therapy, is still understudied.
The proposed project will investigate potential methods to improve electrical integration between engineered graft
tissue and host myocardium, aiming to improve the efficacy and safety of cardiac cell therapy.

title: Anti-citrullinated Protein Antibodies in the Female Reproductive Tract
text:
This research is directly relevant to human health since rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune
disease that disproportionally affects women. This work will advance our understanding of RA etiology by
investigating anti-citrullinated protein antibodies in the female reproductive tract, which is highly relevant to the
NIH-Wide Strategic Plan for Research on the Health of Women.

title: Development of CRISPR/Cas9-based exon-skipping strategies for the treatment of USH-associated deafness
text:
Gene and cell-based therapies using genome editing offer the promise of treatment for a variety of inherited
disorders but has not been used successfully for human hereditary deafness including Usher syndrome. Extraordinary new
tools based on CRISPR/Cas9 based exon-skipping strategies have recently been developed to treat genetic disorders. We
will use these to correct mutations in three different Usher genes that cause inherited hearing loss in humans, using human
inner ear cells and animal models engineered to carry these specific mutations.

title: Computational methods for multiplex image analysis of the tumor microenvironment
text:
The environment in which a tumor develops contains a milieu of different cell types arranged in complex spatial
patterns, where these features may play a critical role in cancer progression and treatment response. We will
develop computational strategies rooted in spatial statistics and deep learning to analyze detailed images of
these tumor microenvironments. This analysis will deepen our understanding on the spatial structure of tumors
and identify patterns that could facilitate individualized treatment decisions.

title: Peptibodies As Novel Therapies in Atrial Fibrillation
text:
Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common heart rhythm disturbance seen in the clinic and is a major cause of morbidity
and mortality. Current treatments for AF are inadequate and are marred by dangerous side effects. Here, we will utilize
protein engineering approaches to provide proof of concept for the design of new therapeutic modalities that are safe and
effective in stopping AF and restoring normal sinus rhythm.

title: The Role of Gardnerella and Prevotella Species as Early Colonizers in the Pathogenesis of Incident Bacterial Vaginosis
text:
Bacterial vaginosis (BV) is the most common vaginal infection worldwide and is associated with an increased
risk of HIV and sexually transmitted infection (STI) acquisition, infertility, preterm birth, and other adverse health
outcomes. The etiology of BV remains unknown; however, Gardnerella and Prevotella species are hypothesized
to be early colonizers of the BV biofilm with synergistic potential. Results from the proposed F31 project will
provide further insight into these bacterial species, their role in the pathogenesis of incident BV, and inform
improvements in BV diagnosis, treatment, and prevention.

title: Statistical Methods for Integrative Analysis of Large-Scale Whole Genome Sequencing Studies and Biobanks of Common Diseases
text:
This project aims to develop and apply advanced statistical methods powered by synthetic data generated from
generative ML/AI models for integrative analysis of large scale whole genome sequencing studies (WGS) and
biobanks. We will improve the power of common and rare variant association studies through synthetic WGS
analysis; develop synthetic and transfer causal medication analysis in the presence of missing omics data and
population heterogeneity to uncover the biological causal pathways of exposure, molecular mediators and diseases
and traits; and develop synthetic and transfer knockoff methods to enhance fine mapping and the identification of
causal variants in multi-ancestry studies. Ultimately, this work will accelerate biological discovery and advance
precision health.

title: Lipid-dependent host-microbe interactions
text:
Lipids are important mediators of signaling with underdefined roles in mediating communication between
mammals and their beneficial gut microbes. Defining key mechanisms governing host-microbe lipid exchange
will allow us to target these exchanges for the benefit of human health.

title: Optimizing the Delivery of Obesity Treatment Through Facilitated Assessment and Selection Strategies
text:
Obesity (body mass index >30 kg/m2) and its associated chronic conditions (e.g., diabetes, hypertension)
represents a major healthcare burden in the United States. While bariatric surgery and the more recently
approved Glucagon-Like-Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists are effective obesity treatments, little is known about
their current individual or combined use at the population level. This study will assess current obesity treatment
use at a population level, what factors contribute to variation in treatment use, as well as design, implement,
and test a tool to help clinicians and patients select, deliver, and use the treatments.

title: Precision Medicine Policy and Treatment (PreEMPT) Model II
text: With hundreds of genetic tests becoming available for clinical use, adding genomic sequencing for all newborns at birth to predict and prevent future diseases is becoming a possibility. Our research aims to extend the Precision Medicine Policy and Treatment (PreEMPT) Model – a sophisticated computer model capable of simulating short- and long-term clinical benefits and estimating the cost-effectiveness of integrating different genomic sequencing strategies into clinical care for newborns for a wide variety of heritable conditions – to evaluate outcomes through adulthood and in testing of siblings of newborns with mutations. We will also identify factors that influence the value of newborn genomic sequencing with the goal of improving medical care and health outcomes for all populations.

title: Mechanical properties of adipose tissue and its effect on breast cancer
text:
Metastasis is the leading cause of death in patients with advanced breast cancer and increases in frequency
with obesity; however, the underlying mechanisms that cause breast cancer metastasis remain unclear. By
iteratively coupling computer simulations, experiments, and advanced omics approaches, the proposed studies
will improve understanding of how obesity-dependent changes in breast adipose tissue mechanical properties
regulate breast cancer invasion and metastasis and link these changes to targetable cellular mechanisms. The
generated new insights have the potential to decrease breast cancer burden associated with the obesity
epidemic in the U.S.

title: Innate immune factors governing restriction of human coronaviruses
text:
Infection with human coronaviruses (HCoVs) causes a wide range of disease outcomes ranging from
mild for endemic viruses like HCoV-OC43, to more lethal for SARS-CoV-2 suggesting there may be
differences in the features of the innate immune response that control infection. The proposed studies
begin to test this hypothesis by comprehensively identifying innate immune factors that control HCoV-
OC43 infection, and by comparatively assessing the activity of immune factors against HCoV-OC43
and SARS-CoV-2 using a series of cell-based studies, as well as biochemical characterization of virus-
host protein interactions. These studies will provide a mechanistic framework to describe differences in
interferon-mediated innate immune responses to diverse coronavirus species and may help to inform
broadly acting therapeutic strategies targeting innate immunity.

title: Data Science
text: The Data Science Shared Resource (DSSR) of the H-H U54 initiative aims to provide comprehensive data support, ensure data integrity, and facilitate FAIR (findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable) data curation. DSSR is co-led by a team of experts from Johns Hopkins University Sidney Kimmel Comprehensive Cancer Center and Howard University, with complementary expertise. The DSSR will implement advanced database technologies, optimize data access, and establish an analytical framework for scientific rigor and reproducibility. The DSSR plans to develop advanced curation tools, incorporate artificial intelligence, and create analytic tools to manage data. The shared resource will also enhance the data model by incorporating attributes relevant to population-based research and developing an analytics infrastructure to support robust and representative data analysis. The DSSR is committed to continuous advancement, promoting collaborative code sharing, and developing models that employ statistical methods, artificial intelligence, and machine learning to deepen scientific understanding and improve cancer research outcomes.

title: Chronic sleep disruption as prognostic biomarker of cognitive recovery following traumatic brain injury.
text:
Disrupted sleep is a common and persistent symptom after traumatic brain injury, which
can significantly complicate recovery. Chronic disturbances in sleep patterns may induce
adverse changes in cognitive performance and over time lead to memory dysfunction.
However, the mechanisms underlying cognitive deficits due to chronic sleep disruption
following traumatic brain injury remain poorly understood. To improve quality of life in
Service Members and Veterans with traumatic brain injury, an understanding of the varied
mechanisms triggered by traumatic brain injury is required to prevent or optimally manage
cognitive recovery over time post injury. Therefore, the goal of this project is to interrogate
chronic sleep disruption and related cognitive deficits using a clinically relevant large
animal model of traumatic brain injury.

title: Mechanisms of Gastrointestinal COVID-19
text:
Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has infected millions, impacted billions of lives, and precipitated
socioeconomic destabilization. There is a pressing need to understand SARS-CoV-2 replicates in the host
gastrointestinal tract, interacts with the mucosal immune system, and drives diarrheal disease. We expect our
results to drive innovative therapeutics to treat COVID-19 related enteric diseases with or without inflammatory
bowel diseases.

title: Integrative Analysis of Lung Cancer Etiology and Risk
text:
Worldwide and in the U.S. lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer mortality. Our proposal identifies risk
factors at each step of lung cancer development to understand the mechanisms controlling and influencing its
progression and to identify biomarkers that can be used clinically for early detection. We have also included
diverse communities in our research program, in order to identify approaches to engage them in risk reduction
strategies.
